# BAD-097 — web/CLAUDE.md and collabweb-sync.js still describe the supersession guard BAD-093 removed

## Brief
BAD-093 narrowed the web's supersession guard so it no longer cancels the arrival pull, but the two places that write that fact down still state the old shape, and neither is in BAD-093's deliverables. web/CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session that touches web/, so a false sentence there is the most expensive kind.

Evidence: web/CLAUDE.md:322-327 says refreshCollab 'abandons everything below its read when a newer refresh overtakes it, which is right for the PAINT and wrong for a TRANSFER, since every other caller passes pull:false and picks up nothing the guard dropped' - that is now only true of renderer/app.js. web/collabweb-sync.js:208-216's comment above runCollabSync's pull says the same thing in the same words, and it is the stated reason that pull is NOT folded into refreshCollab's pull branch; on the web that reason no longer holds, so the next reader can fold it on a rationale the code has retired. Both need the BAD-093 split (web narrowed, desktop not yet, BAD-041 closes the gap) said once, next to the BAD-094 note the test file already carries.

## Size, persona and model decision
One writer, tier overridden to opus. The work is two prose edits and no behaviour change, which is sonnet's shape, but the danger is not the prose: both records reach a conclusion (keep the pull in runCollabSync) whose STATED reason BAD-093 retired, and the surviving reason is a different one — collabSync.busy's exactly-one-transfer-in-flight window. A plausible but wrong replacement sentence in web/CLAUDE.md is loaded into every session that touches web/, which is the expensive kind of error and the reason the tier is not sonnet.

## Outcome
Landed as https://github.com/0snug0/BadTakes/pull/395 (squash 386ae63). Four records, not the three the ticket named, all of which gave refreshCollab's seq guard as the reason runCollabSync owns its pull: web/CLAUDE.md's sync paragraph, the comment above the pull, and two in test/collabreads.test.js, one of them heading a web-executed test. The arrangement stands and the reason is now ownership — collabSync.busy is what exactly-one-transfer-in-flight means, queued folds a mid-cycle transfer into one later run, phase/error are the sync line's report — while refreshCollab is the cycle's read and its pull branch is a different transfer, selectScene's arrival pull, which runs outside that window. Each record now says a fold would no longer LOSE the pull on the web, only put two transfers with different owners on one parameter. The seq claim is kept and scoped to the desktop, where it is still true, pointing at the assertion that pins it; renderer/CLAUDE.md says the same thing and was deliberately left alone as BAD-041's. Also corrected, and not in the ticket: collab:changed was listed among the callers landing in the web's window and is a desktop event with no web counterpart (main.js, preload.js, renderer/app.js only) — an error that predates this ticket and that its own evidence carried into the brief. npm test green on the merged tree (1858 tests, 0 fail); no assertion loosened or re-anchored, one assertion message changed. Eric asked for the merge in this session.
